claim: Social-security disputes go to the social section (cpca 500 ¶7) but do not pass through a conciliation office: Law 08-08 makes a prior internal recourse mandatory (art. 4) and then gives only 30 days from delivery of the notification of the national prior-recourse commission's decision, or 60 days from its receipt of the petition when no reply comes, to bring the case before the court (art. 15). The record knows only the six-month period from a non-conciliation record; for such a claim nonconciliation_record is 'no', so d5 says nothing and the claim falls under d1's fifteen years.

source.what: Law 08-08 of 23 February 2008 on social-security disputes, Official Journal 2008 no. 11 (2 March 2008), p. 8 (art. 2 to 5) and p. 9 (art. 13 to 15). Also cpca 500 ¶7, Official Journal 2008 no. 21, p. 41 (https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/JO-ARABE/2008/A2008021.pdf). Not checked: whether Law 08-08 was amended later; the amendment ledger does not cover it.

quoteArabic: المادة 4 : ترفع الخلافات المتعلقة بالمنازعات العامة إجباريا أمام لجان الطعن المسبق، قبل أي طعن أمام الجهات القضائية. ... المادة 15 : تكون القرارات الصادرة عن اللجنة الوطنية المؤهلة للطعن المسبق قابلة للطعن فيها أمام المحكمة المختصة طبقا لأحكام قانون الإجراءات المدنية، في أجل ثلاثين (30) يوما ابتداء من تاريخ تسليم تبليغ القرار المعترض عليه، أو في أجل ستين (60) يوما ابتداء من تاريخ استلام العريضة من طرف اللجنة الوطنية المؤهلة للطعن المسبق إذا لم يتلق المعني أي رد على عريضته.
consequence: A social-security claim (insured person or employer against a social-security body) has its own 30-day or 60-day filing period and a mandatory prior recourse; the record gives it no deadline and, through d1, a fifteen-year horizon. A lawyer would be told nothing while a 30-day period runs out. The record must at least recognise this case and not treat 'no non-conciliation record' as 'no filing deadline' for the social section.

claim: The Civil Code itself sets a three-year limitation for every action arising from an insurance contract, running from the event that gave rise to it (art. 624), with its own delayed starting points (concealment or false declaration: from the insurer's knowledge; occurrence of the insured event: from the knowledge of those concerned). The record does not cite it; an insured person's claim against his insurer is answered by d1 (fifteen years from the due date), so a claim three to fifteen years old gets no warning at all.

source.what: Ordinance 75-58 of 26 September 1975 (Civil Code), art. 624, Official Journal 1975 no. 78 (30 September 1975), Arabic p. 1030; French edition p. 849 (https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/JO-FRANCAIS/1975/F1975078.pdf: « Les actions nées du contrat d'assurance se prescrivent par trois années à partir de la date de l'événement qui leur a donné naissance »). Art. 624 is not in the amendment ledger. Lead, not read: Ordinance 95-07 on insurance (art. 27) is said to set the same three years.

quoteArabic: المادة 624 : تسقط بالتقادم الدعاوى الناشئة عن عقد التأمين بانقضاء ثلاث سنوات من وقت حدوث الواقعة التي تولدت عنها هذه الدعاوى. غير انه لا تسرى تلك المدة : - فى حالة اخفاء بيانات متعلقة بالخطر المؤمن منه أو تقديم بيانات غير صحيحة أو غير دقيقة عن هذا الخطر الا من اليوم الذى علم فيه المؤمن بذلك. - فى حالة وقوع الحادث المؤمن منه الا من اليوم الذى علم فيه ذوو الشأن بوقوعه.
consequence: Insurance-contract claims need their own deadline (three years from the generating event, with the two knowledge-based starts) or at least a question that takes them out of d1; as written, d1's fifteen years is wrong for them and the record is silent until fifteen years have passed.

claim: CPCA 504 forfeits the right to sue once six months from delivery of the record have run; the only way back is an order lifting the forfeiture (cpca 322), and the only extension is to the next working day when the last day is not one (cpca 405 ¶4). The record applies its 15-day warning band after expiry too, so a claim filed several working days late is shown only as a warning: ex19 (record delivered 2025-10-20, petition 2026-04-25) expects 'warn', although the last day (20/21 April 2026, Monday/Tuesday) is an ordinary working day and no reading of o4 or o7 saves it.

source.what: Law 08-09 of 25 February 2008 (CPCA), art. 504, Official Journal 2008 no. 21 (23 April 2008), p. 41. Art. 504 is not touched by Law 22-13 (amendment ledger).

quoteArabic: المادة 504 : يجب رفع الدعوى أمام القسم الاجتماعي في أجل لا يتجاوز ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح، وذلك تحت طائلة سقوط الحق في رفع الدعوى.
consequence: After the last possible day under every recorded reading (day of delivery and day of expiry both excluded, then extended past any non-working day), d5 should block the clean export, not warn; the band can only cover the days the open points o4 and o7 make uncertain, not a fixed 15 days after expiry. ex19 expects the wrong effect.

claim: The Commercial Code is said to set short limitation periods for bills of exchange and cheques: three years from maturity for actions against the acceptor of a bill, one year and six months for recourse between holders and endorsers (art. 461), and six months from the end of the presentment period for the holder's recourse on a cheque (art. 527 or near). A claim for payment of an unpaid bill or cheque is answered by d1 with fifteen years.

source.what: My own memory of Ordinance 75-59 of 26 September 1975 (Commercial Code), arts. 461 and 527 (article numbers and wording not verified; not read on joradp.dz, Official Journal 1975 no. 101 not fetched). A lead only.

quoteArabic: (from memory, unverified) تتقادم كل الدعاوى الناتجة عن السفتجة ضد القابل بمضي ثلاث سنوات اعتبارا من تاريخ الاستحقاق
consequence: o9's protective reading (apply 308 and warn that a shorter period may apply) is only shown when d1 itself fires, i.e. after fifteen years; for bills and cheques the warning comes years too late. Check arts. 461 and 527 of the Commercial Code on the Official Journal and add them or a question that excludes these claims from d1.

claim: Code of Criminal Procedure art. 10 is said to provide that the civil action follows the Civil Code's limitation but may no longer be brought before the criminal court once the public action is time-barred. A victim of a harmful act that is also an offence (assault, road accident) therefore has a much shorter window for the civil-party route than d2's fifteen years.

source.what: My own memory of Ordinance 66-155 (Code of Criminal Procedure), art. 10 as amended (amending law not identified, not read on joradp.dz). A lead only.

quoteArabic: (from memory, unverified) تتقادم الدعوى المدنية وفق أحكام القانون المدني، غير أنه لا يجوز رفع هذه الدعوى أمام الجهة القضائية الجزائية بعد انقضاء أجل تقادم الدعوى العمومية.
consequence: This app files before the civil courts, so d2 stands for the petition itself; but d2's message should not let the lawyer believe fifteen years also holds for a civil-party claim before the criminal court. Verify art. 10 on the Official Journal.

claim: The French edition of art. 310 names more creditors than the Arabic one the record follows: dental surgeons, midwives and architects (« chirurgiens-dentistes, sages-femmes ... architectes »). The question for claim_is_professional_fees reads out a closed Arabic list; a lawyer for a midwife or an architect will likely answer 'no', and d6's two years is then replaced by d1's fifteen.

source.what: Ordinance 75-58 (Civil Code), art. 310, Official Journal 1975 no. 78, French edition p. 832; Arabic edition of the same issue (https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/JO-ARABE/1975/A1975078.pdf) as quoted in the record (b4). The Arabic text is the official one; the gap is narrow (dentists are arguably doctors, architects arguably engineers).

quoteArabic: تتقادم بسنتين حقوق الاطباء، والصيادلة، والمحامين، والمهندسين والخبراء ، ووكلاء التفليسة ، والسماسرة، والاساتذة، والمعلمين
consequence: The question should not read as a closed list that a dentist's, architect's or midwife's lawyer would answer 'no' to; at least the record should note the French list and that d1 then gives a period seven times too long.
